name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details better than standard upscalers, giving a measurable quality bump in final outputs. The trade-off is slower processing—depth-aware upscaling adds 10-15% runtime—so we’ll run it only on keyframes.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem is motion-induced blur, not resolution loss—depth maps can’t recover lost facial details from motion. Instead, test Flowframes’ VFI with a strict A/B: run EXCAVA’s output through Flowframes’ motion interpolation, then compare face fidelity scores against the original. If the score improves by ≥0.5%, adopt it; if not, the bottleneck is elsewhere.

name: Gearbox

Add Flowframes’ VFI module to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. Motion blur in source frames is the bottleneck, not resolution—depth-aware upscaling can’t fix what’s already smeared. The trade-off is a 5-8% runtime increase, but that’s cheaper than wasting compute on upscaling blurry inputs.

name: Torque
text: Flowframes’ VFI won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it’s tuned for smooth motion, not preserving identity—reconstructed faces blur or distort when source frames are already smeared. Test Real-ESRGAN’s face-specific model instead; if it recovers lost details better than Flowframes in a blind A/B, we’ll know the core problem is resolution loss, not motion blur.
